chapter: New Orleans bands, brass bands and learning bass
title: Quadrilles and Creole dance figures
summary: Quadrilles and mazurkas, the called figures, and 'Bachaca' as the Creole word for swinging out.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What about quadrilles and mazurkas and things like that? How do you count them?
You don't know nothing about quadrilles.
I'm going to hear one Friday night.
Yeah, they're going to have one at the festival.
I'll have to play a quadrilles in the charters.
Well, I tell you. You want to go to rehearsal?
I don't know. I'll call the ladies if you want to when we're finished. All right. The ladies run those kind of dances, you know.
Oh, they run the quadrilles dance. Yeah, that's what I mean. Yeah, well, they're the same as the old timers running a reel. Yeah, they have a-
Call the figures, you know. Yeah. But here, we have three figures of the old quadrilles. First, second, third, and the fourth. What do you call it?

I mean, swing your partner. Oh. Make me get out there and want to do a little dancing. You know anything about Bachaca? Who? Bachaca. That's what you call it when they swing out. Swing? That's what they call it in Creole.
I think that's what they say.
I don't speak Creole very well. I see.
